newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, May 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, May 2.

text.p: The following are the highlights of stories from the Irish press on Friday.
- Tony Blair swept sensationally to power this morning with a record-breaking landslide election victory as the British people took dire revenge on the Conservatives after 18 years in power.
- Mortgage rates will increase next week after the Central Bank raised wholesale interest rates by half a percentage point yesterday.
- A murder investigation is under way in Kilkenny after the body of a middle-aged man was found battered to death in the grounds of a religious retreat home.

- The latest events in the currency and interest rate markets have sparked strong Opposition criticism of finance minister Ruairi Quinn and have led analysts to question the direction of currency and interest rates policy.
- A tidal wave of support swept Britain's Labour leader Tony Blair into Downing Street today.

- An increase of one percent in bank and mortgage rates was threatened last night after a shock rise in Central Bank rates. - Police were last night investigating three violent deaths - a homeless man beaten about the head with a wooden stake and an elderly couple who died from shotgun wounds.
- Etain Doyle has been appointed Ireland's first director of telecommunications regulation after a period working as a consultant with ESB International.

- Home loans will cost more within days following yesterday's surprise 0.5 percent increase in Central Bank interest rates. - A man was arrested in Dublin last night for questioning following the discovery of the battered body of a 46-year old man in Kilkenny city.
- Labour leader Tony Blair will cross the threshold of 10 Downing Street today and become Britain's first Labour prime minister in 18 years.

- Irish finance minister Ruairi Quinn rejected charges that he was to blame for speculator attacks on the pound which led to the Central Bank delivering an unwelcome pre-election rise in interest rates.
